concept.name: Loan-to-value ratio
concept.definition: Loan-to-value (LTV) is the ratio of the borrowed amount to the value of the collateral securing it; in DeFi lending, each asset's maximum LTV caps how much can be newly borrowed against it.
concept.intuition: LTV is the leverage dial on a collateralized loan: 75% LTV means every $100 of collateral backs at most $75 of new borrowing.
concept.mechanics: In Aave, a user's maximum borrowing power is Σ(collateral value × asset LTV); opening a borrow that would exceed it reverts. LTV is set per asset by governance below the liquidation threshold, leaving a buffer so borrowers are not instantly liquidatable at max borrow; E-Mode categories raise LTV for correlated pairs (e.g. stablecoins at 97%).
concept.formula: LTV = borrow value / collateral value; max borrow = Σ (collateral_i × price_i × LTV_i).
concept.failure_modes: Borrowing at maximum LTV leaves almost no buffer: a small adverse price move or accrued interest pushes the position to liquidation; LTV does not protect against oracle mispricing of the collateral itself.
concept.misconceptions: A higher max LTV is not 'better collateral' in economic terms — it is a risk parameter choice trading capital efficiency against liquidation safety. LTV caps new borrows; the liquidation threshold, a separate higher number, triggers liquidations.
concept.example: With $10,000 of ETH collateral at 75% LTV you can borrow up to $7,500; if ETH's liquidation threshold is 80%, your loan becomes liquidatable only once debt exceeds $8,000 (through price drops or interest).

citations.source: Frangella & Herskind, Aave V3 Technical Paper (2022)
citations.section: Section 3-4: risk parameters (LTV, liquidation threshold, liquidation bonus)
